newsitem.title: NAMIBIA: Namibian petrol prices cut by five cents a litre.
newsitem.headline: Namibian petrol prices cut by five cents a litre.

text.p: Petrol and diesel prices in Namibia are to fall by five cents a litre on Wednesday, the ministry of mines and energy announced on Tuesday.

"For the second consecutive quarter the pump prices of controlled petroleum products, petrol and diesel, will be decreasing with effect from 16 July 1997", minister Andimba Toivo ya Toivo said in a statement.
"The reason for this decrease is the favourable import parity situation brought about by the recent fall in international crude oil and product prices," he said.
He said lower international prices had more than offset the decline in the value of the currency against the dollar, the currency of world oil trade.
Along with the reduction in pump prices, the ministry also announced a small increase in the dealer margin of 0.5 cents a litre to "enhance the economic viability of the service station sector".
The changes mean that in Walvisbay leaded and unleaded petrol will now cost N$1.90 a litre, in Windhoek N$2.00, Keetmanshoop N$2.09 and in Oshakati and Katima Mulilo N$2.04.
